teaser.text: Aflac sells insurance that pays cash when illness, injury, disability or death meets the policy’s rules. Its business is a long financial exchange: customers pay premiums now, Aflac invests much of that money, and the company pays claims and expenses later.

stock.title: Aflac stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Aflac’s stock forecast weighs Japan runoff, U.S. claims, investment income, capital returns and valuation across bear, base and bull cases.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast reaches $127.93 by October 2029, a 13% return. It hinges on Japan stabilizing and U.S. claims normalizing.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Aflac’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Aflac's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted case is $117.39 in October 2027, roughly 0% return. It reaches $127.93 in October 2029, a 13% return. Bear carries 30% probability and base 55%. Bull carries 15%.

The range is much wider than the weighted path. By October 2029, the bear case reaches $64.45 while the bull case reaches $193.37, against today’s $119.97. The base case is the most likely outcome, but the downside is severe if operating pressure and valuation compression reinforce each other.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Aflac?

paragraphs.text: Book value starts from $30,312 million, the latest reported common equity. The base case assumes $4,000 million of annual core earnings. Dividends are $1,300 million and buybacks $3,000 million, producing a modest decline because 2025 core earnings were $4,008 million while distributions were substantial. The bear case adds a large market or reserve shock, uses lower earnings and slower repurchases, and reaches $24,312 million by 2029. The bull case assumes $4,500 million of earnings, selective buybacks and favorable marks, reaching $30,512 million. The bear reflects reserve, rate and investment volatility; the bull reflects stronger investment income and capital retention.

blocks.heading: How much does Aflac really earn and return?

paragraphs.text: Insurance cash flow cannot be read like an industrial company’s free cash flow. Premiums and investment income fund claims, while reserves accumulate for benefits that may arrive years later. Capital held inside regulated subsidiaries and the ability to remit dividends matter more than a simple subtraction of capital spending.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Aflac today?

paragraphs.text: A P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, shows how much investors pay for each dollar of earnings. A trailing P/E uses the last 12 months; a forward P/E uses expected earnings; and core earnings remove specified investment and other items. In Q2 2026, reported diluted EPS was $1.63, while adjusted diluted EPS was $1.75. Investment results caused much of the gap, so the underlying insurance business had not changed as sharply as reported earnings suggested.

dividend.title: Aflac dividend: payout and cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: Aflac pays a growing dividend, but the latest payout exceeded common earnings, so coverage depends on subsidiary cash and capital needs.
dividend.opening: Aflac currently pays $0.61 per quarter and has a record of annual increases. The latest year paid out more to common shareholders than it earned, so dividend coverage depends on subsidiary cash generation and capital needs.
dividend.closing: The full Aflac memo also covers Aflac’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Aflac pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The dividend base case rises from the current $0.61 quarterly rate to the measured annual increases shown in the table. The bear freezes the payout at $2.44 per share because Japan’s runoff, U.S. claims and capital demands could make the board cautious. The bull reaches $3.00 because higher investment income and subsidiary remittances support faster increases. Aflac’s 43-year record of annual increases supports the base, but 2025 distributions exceeded net income.

blocks.heading: Does Aflac’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The payout therefore needs context. In the latest year, Aflac paid out more to common shareholders than it earned for them. That does not automatically signal distress because an insurer can use capital accumulated earlier, but it does make buybacks discretionary rather than guaranteed. The central test is whether subsidiary cash generation can support shareholder returns without weakening the insurance operation.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management expects Japan underlying earned premiums to decline 1% to 2%. It expects U.S. net earned premium growth just below 3%. Its 2025–2027 U.S. target is a 3% to 6% CAGR. It targets annualized subsidiary dividends of $2,400 million to $3,000 million, subject to regulated subsidiaries’ remittances.

The view moves toward bear if Japan’s APIF and earned premiums deteriorate through 2027–2029, or if sales rise without replacing paid-up policies. Persistent U.S. benefit-ratio pressure during 2027–2028 would weaken margins and earnings.
